title: GERUNDIO o INFINITIVO
subtitle: Verb + -ing or verb + to · ¿doing o to do?

map.center: Cuando un verbo va detrás de otro, el segundo va en -⁠ing (enjoy doing) o con to (want to do).

nodes.title: Verbo + -ING
items: enjoy, finish, avoid, mind, suggest, keep, miss…

nodes.title: Verbo + TO
items: want, decide, hope, need, plan, learn, promise…

nodes.title: Preposición + -ING
items: Tras in, at, of, for, without, before… → -⁠ing

nodes.title: -ING como sujeto

nodes.title: Truco
items: to → mira al futuro: want, hope, plan, decide
-⁠ing → la actividad en sí: enjoy, finish, avoid

items.q: I enjoy ____ films.
She wants ____ abroad.
He's good at ____.
____ is my favourite sport.
We decided ____ a taxi.

explain.es: Cuando en una frase hay dos verbos seguidos, el primero «manda» sobre la forma del segundo. Unos verbos piden -ing (I enjoy dancing) y otros piden to + infinitivo (I want to dance). En español casi siempre usamos el infinitivo («disfruto bailando», «quiero bailar»), así que en inglés hay que aprender qué pide cada verbo. Además, detrás de una preposición y como sujeto se usa siempre -ing.
explain.en: When two verbs go together, the first one decides the form of the second: -ing (enjoy dancing) or to + infinitive (want to dance).

explain.title: 1 · Verbos + -ING
explain.es: Estos verbos van seguidos de -ing: enjoy (disfrutar), finish (terminar), avoid (evitar), mind (importar), suggest (sugerir), keep (seguir, no parar de), miss (echar de menos), practise (practicar), imagine, consider, can't stand (no soportar). ¡Detrás de ellos nunca va to!
explain.en: These verbs are followed by -ing: enjoy, finish, avoid, mind, suggest, keep, miss, practise, imagine, consider, can't stand.

examples.en: I really enjoy cooking for my friends.
examples.es: Disfruto mucho cocinando para mis amigos.

examples.en: She avoids eating sugar during the week.

explain.title: 2 · Verbos + TO
explain.es: Estos verbos van seguidos de to + infinitivo: want (querer), decide (decidir), hope (esperar, desear), need (necesitar), plan (planear), learn (aprender), promise (prometer), agree (acordar), refuse (negarse), forget (olvidarse de), try (intentar), would like (me gustaría). Muchos miran hacia el futuro: algo que todavía no ha pasado.
explain.en: These verbs take to + infinitive: want, decide, hope, need, plan, learn, promise, agree, refuse, forget, try, would like.

examples.en: We decided to book a cheaper hotel.
examples.es: Decidimos reservar un hotel más barato.

examples.en: I hope to see you again soon!

explain.title: Truco: ¿hacia delante o la acción?
explain.es: Muchos verbos con to miran hacia el futuro: want, hope, plan, decide, promise, would like (algo que aún no ha pasado). Muchos verbos con -ing hablan de la actividad en sí: enjoy, finish, avoid, mind, keep. No es una regla perfecta, ¡pero ayuda! Y detrás de preposición… siempre -ing.
explain.en: to often looks to the future (want, hope, plan). -ing often refers to the activity itself (enjoy, finish, avoid). After prepositions: always -ing.

explain.title: Las dos listas
head: 🏃 + -ING
Significado
🎯 + TO
Significado
explain.note: Aprende cada verbo con su pareja: enjoy doing, want to do. ¡Como si fuera una sola palabra!
explain.note_en: Learn each verb with its pattern: enjoy doing, want to do.

explain.title: 3 · Preposición + -ING
explain.es: Detrás de cualquier preposición (in, on, at, of, about, for, with, without, before, after, by, instead of) el verbo va siempre en -ing. Aquí el español usa infinitivo («antes de salir», «gracias por venir»), y por eso el error típico es before to leave. Ojo con look forward to: ¡ese to es preposición!
explain.en: After any preposition use -ing: before leaving, thanks for coming, good at drawing. Careful: look forward to + -ing.

examples.es: Lávate las manos antes de comer.

explain.title: 4 · -ING como sujeto
explain.es: Cuando una actividad es el sujeto de la frase, en inglés usamos -ing (y el verbo va en singular). En español usamos el infinitivo: «Nadar es sano» → Swimming is healthy. ¡No digas Swim is healthy!
explain.en: When an activity is the subject, use -ing: Swimming is healthy. Reading helps you relax.

examples.es: Nadar es bueno para la espalda.

examples.en: Getting up early is really hard for me.

explain.title: 5 · LIKE, LOVE, HATE
explain.es: Like, love, hate y prefer pueden ir con -ing o con to casi sin diferencia: I love dancing = I love to dance. Para gustos generales, -ing es lo más natural. ¡Pero ojo con would like / would love! Esas van siempre con to: I'd like to go (me gustaría ir).
explain.en: like, love, hate, prefer + -ing or to (same meaning). would like / would love + to only.

examples.en: I love going to concerts with my friends.
examples.es: Me encanta ir a conciertos con mis amigos.

examples.en: She hates getting up early on Mondays.
Would you like to come for dinner on Friday?
examples.es: ¿Te gustaría venir a cenar el viernes?

explain.title: Preposición + -ING: expresiones útiles
head: Expresión
Significado
Ejemplo · Example
rows: I look forward to seeing you.
Walk instead of taking the bus.
explain.note: «Pensar en mudarme» → thinking of moving. ¡Ojo, la preposición no siempre coincide con la del español!
explain.note_en: The preposition is not always the same as in Spanish.

explain.title: STOP y REMEMBER
explain.es: Unos pocos verbos admiten las dos formas, pero cambian de significado. Los dos más útiles son stop y remember:
explain.en: A few verbs take both forms with a different meaning: stop and remember.

items.es: Mira la palabra que va justo delante del segundo verbo.
items.en: Look at the word just before the second verb.

items.es: ¿Es un verbo de la lista -ing (enjoy, finish, avoid, mind…)? → -ing.
¿Es un verbo de la lista to (want, decide, hope, need…) o would like? → to + infinitivo.
items.en: want, decide, hope, would like… → to.

items.es: ¿La actividad es el sujeto de la frase? → -ing (Reading is fun).

lines.en: Have you decided what to do this summer?
Yes! I want to do a language course in Dublin. I'm really looking forward to going.
lines.es: ¡Sí! Quiero hacer un curso de idiomas en Dublín. Tengo muchísimas ganas de ir.

lines.en: Cool! But do you enjoy studying in summer?
lines.es: ¡Qué bien! ¿Pero te gusta estudiar en verano?

lines.en: I don't mind studying if I can practise speaking with real people.
lines.es: No me importa estudiar si puedo practicar la conversación con gente de verdad.

lines.en: I'm thinking of getting a summer job. I need to save some money.
lines.es: Yo estoy pensando en buscar un trabajo de verano. Necesito ahorrar algo de dinero.

lines.en: Good idea. Working in summer is a great experience.
lines.es: Buena idea. Trabajar en verano es una gran experiencia.

lines.en: Yeah, but I hate getting up early!
Then avoid applying for jobs in bakeries!

exercises.title: Lee y contesta
exercises.es: Lee el texto. Marca T (verdadero) o F (falso) y contesta las preguntas con frases completas.
exercises.en: Read the text. Tick T or F and answer the questions.
text: I'm Lucía, and last year I decided to try something new. I was tired of spending every evening on the sofa, and I wanted to meet new people. A friend suggested going to a climbing wall near my flat, so I agreed to go with her one Friday.

At first I was terrible! I'm afraid of falling, and I couldn't stop looking down. But the instructors kept encouraging me, and I decided to go back every week. Climbing is hard, but I really enjoy solving each wall like a puzzle.

Now I can't imagine living without it. Climbing has helped me feel stronger and more confident. Next summer, I'm hoping to climb outdoors in the Picos de Europa. I'm really looking forward to trying it!

items.q: Lucía wanted to meet new people.
Her friend suggested going to a climbing wall.
At first she was very good at climbing.
She isn't afraid of falling.
What was she tired of?
items.a: She was tired of spending every evening on the sofa.

items.q: What does she enjoy about climbing?
items.a: She enjoys solving each wall like a puzzle.

items.q: What is she hoping to do next summer?
items.a: She's hoping to climb outdoors in the Picos de Europa.

items.q: Find two verbs + -ing and two verbs + to in the text.
items.a: -ing: suggested going, kept encouraging, enjoy solving, imagine living. to: decided to try, wanted to meet, agreed to go, hoping to climb.

exercises.title: Ahora escribe tú
exercises.es: Escribe sobre ti. Usa -ing y to.

items.q: Escribe 2 cosas que disfrutas y 1 que no soportas: I enjoy… / I can't stand…
items.a: Ej.: I enjoy playing padel and watching series. I can't stand waiting in queues.

items.q: Escribe 2 planes con want to / hope to / I'm planning to.
items.a: Ej.: I want to learn Italian. I'm planning to visit my cousins in August.

items.q: Termina: I'm really good at… but I'm not very good at…
items.a: Ej.: I'm really good at swimming, but I'm not very good at singing.

items.q: Da un consejo para estudiar mejor con -ing como sujeto.
items.a: Ej.: Sleeping well is very important before an exam.

checklist.es: Sé qué verbos van con -ing: enjoy, finish, avoid, mind…
checklist.en: I know the verbs that take -ing.

checklist.es: Sé qué verbos van con to: want, decide, hope, need…
checklist.en: I know the verbs that take to.

checklist.es: Detrás de una preposición uso -ing: before leaving.
Uso -ing como sujeto: Swimming is fun.
Sé que would like va siempre con to.
Digo look forward to seeing, no to see.
